newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - April 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - April 15.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Hindustan Times
CONGRESS DECIDES TO BACK UNITED FRONT AGAIN

The Congress party unanimously decided to restore support to the United Front (UF) for the formation of a new government. It also decided to withdraw its claim to form the government before the president as soon as the UF elected a new leader to replace Deve Gowda. In a show of total unity under the leadership of Sitaram Kesri, the Congress also decided not to impose any condition on the UF for any role for the Congress in the government at this stage.
Indian Express
MOOPANAR EMERGES FRONT RUNNER FOR PRIME MINISTER'S POST

With Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda having agreed to step down as the leader of the United Front (UF), the search was now on for a successor, possibly by Sunday. A hard stand taken by four regional parties was believed to have made an otherwise obdurate Gowda agree to step down. G.K. Moopanar once again emerged a front-runner for the top slot. The Left parties were also expected to favour him.
The Economic Times
POWER PROJECTS INVOLVING FOREIGN INVESTMENT UNDER REVIEW

The Foreign Investment Promotion Board (FIPB) was reviewing 35 large power projects involving foreign investment, including the seven fast track ones. Among other things, FIPB has sought progress reports on land acquisition and status of power purchase agreements, fuel linkages and financial closure. The feedback from the private power developers had already started pouring in. The FIPB initiative followed reports that several mega power projects with, foreign collaborations are still on paper, even years after they received Foreign Direct Investment approval.
TELECOM DEPARTMENT TO DEFEND NEW CELLULAR TARIFFS

The Department of Telecommunications (DoT) would defend the new fixed to cellular call tariffs which the industry considered to be very high. DoT's argument was that the new tariffs were necessary so that the long distance traffic was not routed through the networks of the private cellular operators. This practice was followed almost all over the world.
Financial Express
BHARATIYA JANATA PARTY BACKS CORPORATE TAX SOPS IN BUDGET

The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) does not oppose the corporate tax reliefs announced in the budget for 1997/98 but would press for a hike in the income tax limit for the salaried class. The party would oppose the imposition of service tax, dereservation and raising of investment limit in the small scale industries sector and the proposal to widen the tax net. Under the budget proposals, persons owning cars, telephone connections and going on foreign travel would normally fall within the tax slabs and should file their tax returns voluntarily. BJP wants this proposal to be spiked.
FEMA FIXES PENALTY AT DOUBLE THE AMOUNT OF VIOLATION

The proposed Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA) will charge the offenders with cash penalties from a minimum of 10,000 rupees to double the amount involved in contravention plus imprisonment up to six months. The proposed act would take away much of the powers of the enforcement directorate and would deal with sale and purchase of foreign exchange, current and capital account transactions and, repatriation of funds to India by exporters. Once FEMA was passed the enforcement directorate could investigate only those cases which were referred to it by the Reserve Bank of India.
